findings.note: Spec/code drift plus a dead injected dependency. This spec states that cmdexec takes its DurationMS from the runner's measured Result.Duration and has 'no Clock'. The shipped struct does declare a Clock field, and internal/fsm/cli/deps.go:90 populates it (Clock: now) when constructing the guarded runner -- but nothing in internal/fsm/cmdexec ever reads it (grep for 'Clock' in the package returns only the declaration). So the codebase carries an injected seam that is wired at the call site and silently ignored, while the spec of record says the seam should not exist. No behavioural bug today, but a future reader wiring a fake clock for cmd timing would get no effect and no error, and 100% statement coverage cannot catch it because a struct field is not a statement. Either drop the field and its assignment, or make the spec sentence match.

evidence.note: Spec text: "DurationMS comes from the runner's measured Result.Duration (no `Clock`)."
Guarded declares 'Clock func() time.Time'; it is the only occurrence of Clock in the package, so the field is never read.
The guarded-runner factory sets Clock: now on cmdexec.Guarded, wiring a dependency the callee ignores.

findings.note: Ordered-list numbering in section 4.2 is out of sequence and survives from the previous plan's review of this same file: the pre-flight step is written as '0.' but placed after item '1.' in source order. Markdown renderers renumber ordered lists sequentially, so the rendered spec shows pre-flight as the second step, contradicting its own 'before any call' / 'with no spend' requirement -- the one ordering property the item exists to state. Move the pre-flight item above item 1.
